article.headline: Herro's homecoming debut fuels Bucks against injury-hit Bulls in Milwaukee
article.summary: Tyler Herro makes his home debut for the Milwaukee Bucks against the Chicago Bulls on Wednesday at 4:10 p.m. ET after scoring 24 points in Milwaukee's 128-116 loss to Washington, while the Bulls arrive fresh off a 135-92 rout by Toronto.
article.body:
Tyler Herro's return to his home state figures to draw attention Wednesday night at Fiserv Forum. The Milwaukee product, acquired in the Giannis trade, scored 24 points and nine assists in the Bucks' season-opening loss to Washington. Now he faces Norman Powell, the All-Star signing who was supposed to share Miami's backcourt with Herro last season but never consistently played alongside him due to injuries.

The Bucks are without Giannis Antetokounmpo on the roster for the first time since the 2012-13 season. Head coach Taylor Jenkins looks to bounce back after his team surrendered a 128-116 defeat despite leading 96-90 in the fourth quarter. Jaime Jaquez Jr. added 22 points and seven rebounds in that loss.

Chicago arrives bruised. The Bulls suffered the most lopsided defeat in a season opener in franchise history, losing 135-92 to Toronto while giving up 43 first-quarter points. Matas Buzelis led Chicago with 17 points, but rookie Caleb Wilson scored 16 while committing nine turnovers. Point guard Josh Giddey managed only 1-for-10 shooting and is probable with a wrist injury. Zach Collins is also probable with a right quadriceps strain.

The Bucks trail Chicago 138-137 all-time in regular season meetings but won three of four last season, capturing both home contests. Chicago's most recent victory came March 1 with a 120-97 win, as Giddey posted a triple-double.

article.headline: Wind wreaks havoc at Portman Road as Ipswich host struggling Forest
article.summary: Ipswich Town face Nottingham Forest in a Premier League match at Portman Road where strong wind conditions are affecting play, with Forest having failed to score in four top-flight games this season.
article.body:
Strong wind at Portman Road is already shaping the contest, holding up goalkeeper Walton's kicks from his own area and sending Gibbs-White's knock out of play in the opening minutes. The conditions are turning into a factor both teams must manage.

Nottingham Forest arrive with a glaring weakness in attack. The visiting side has failed to score in four different Premier League games this season—more than any other team in the top flight. Manager Oliver Glasner acknowledged the issue this week, saying "I don't see it as a massive problem because we're creating enough situations," though Forest supporters may be less convinced.

The problem centers on the club's £45m summer signing from Chelsea, Liam Delap. While Delap scored with his third shot for Forest this term, he has since managed only one goal in his last 15 attempts. Ipswich's top scorer from their previous Premier League campaign in 2024-25, Delap was brought in as a key attacking addition but has struggled to replicate his early impact as the season has progressed.

The match unfolds amid these attacking difficulties for Forest, with Ipswich hosting at home where conditions are proving unpredictable.

news.og_title: رياضي/ رئيس الاتحاد الآسيوي لكرة القدم يؤكد مواصلة دعم الاتحادات الوطنية والإقليمية
news.og_desc:
طوكيو 11 جمادى الأولى 1448 هـ  الموافق 22 أكتوبر 2026 م  واس
    أكد الشيخ سلمان بن إبراهيم آل خليفة رئيس الاتحاد الآسيوي لكرة القدم، التزام الاتحاد بمواصلة دعم الاتحادات الوطنية والإقليمية الأعضاء، والعمل معها لتمكينها من تحقيق طموحاتها والارتقاء بمعايير الاحتراف والحوكمة في كرة القدم الآسيوية.
    جاء ذلك خلال ختام النسخة الرابعة لمؤتمر رؤساء وأمناء عامي الاتحادات الوطنية والإقليمية الأعضاء في الاتحاد الآسيوي لكرة القدم 2026، الذي أقيم في العاصمة اليابانية طوكيو على مدى يومين، وشهد نقاشات وتبادل الخبرات والرؤى حول مستقبل كرة القدم في القارة.
    وأشار إلى أن المؤتمر شكل منصة مهمة لاستعراض النجاحات المحققة واستكشاف آفاق جديدة للتقدم والتطوير بما يسهم في الارتقاء بكرة القدم الآسيوية، مؤكدًا أن النقاشات التي شهدها المؤتمر ستعود بالفائدة على مستقبل اللعبة في القارة.
    وأوضح أن المؤتمر استهدف تبادل الأفكار وتوسيع قاعدة المعرفة وتعزيز العلاقات المهنية بين القيادات الكروية الآسيوية، معربًا عن ثقته في تحقيق هذه الأهداف، ومجددًا التأكيد أن الاتحادات الوطنية والإقليمية الأعضاء تقع في صميم عمل الاتحاد الآسيوي وأولوياته.
    وشدد رئيس الاتحاد الآسيوي على مواصلة العمل عن كثب مع الاتحادات الأعضاء، من خلال تعزيز قدراتها وتوفير الأدوات اللازمة لمساعدتها على المحافظة على أعلى معايير الاحتراف والحوكمة، بما يدعم مسيرة التطوير المستدام لكرة القدم الآسيوية.
    // انتهى //
